target.statement: For every fixed finite number N of section-valued agents over a finite lattice or a compact contextual base with a refining lattice family, construct an ELBO-founded PIFB2 theory in which fast belief sections q_i are recognition densities, slow model sections s_i are typed parameter-recognition laws or deterministic parameters, and transported peer interactions use KL(q_i||(Omega_ij)_#q_j); distinguish exact time-lagged conditional, configuration-law, and emergent empirical-measure realizations; begin with arbitrary compact closed subgroups of GL(K,R), and state the additional obligations for a full GL(K,R) extension and for deterministic or process-law continuum limits.
target.quantifiers: For every fixed finite N >= 1; lattice refinement h->0 is separate from any later N->infinity limit.
domains: Finite oriented lattice or compact contextual base with a declared refining lattice family.
Fast recognition-density sections q_i and slow model/parameter sections s_i.
Closed compact subgroups G of GL(K,R), with full GL(K,R) treated as an extension.
codomains: Exact finite-lattice ELBOs, effective actions, and conditional continuum functionals.
target.regularity: Dominated positive laws for displayed KL terms; smooth or Sobolev sections and regular meshes for continuum statements.
measures: Declared state, parameter, base, link, and configuration reference measures.
boundary_conditions: Periodic or explicitly retained Dirichlet/Neumann boundary sectors.
symmetries: Passive gauge covariance under the declared representation and relabeling covariance of finite agents.
target.equivalence: Actions modulo additive observation-dependent constants and passive gauge equivalence; dynamical and equilibrium constructions are not identified without an invariant-measure theorem.
premises: Microscopic laws used for exact ELBO claims are normalized and independent of the contemporaneous variational law.
The transported peer law is the pushforward (Omega_ij)_#q_j.
PIFB2 and MAgent are model-selection intuitions, not derivational premises.
modeling_postulates: Beliefs q are fast relative to model variables s in the intended regime.
permitted_theorems: KL chain rule for finite mixtures and standard-Borel disintegration.
Gibbs variational principle with proper reference and finite partition function.
Haar averaging for compact linear groups.
Singular-perturbation and Gamma-convergence results only after their hypotheses are mapped.
target.falsification_criterion: A normalization, typing, contemporaneous-recognition dependence, stability, residual, compactness, or gauge-coercivity failure defeats the corresponding claim.
target.literature_policy: Use current live manuscripts for project status and primary sources for external terminology and theorems.
